title: NASA’s Europa Clipper Zooming by Earth on Way to Jupiter’s Icy Moon
supports: News report published 25 Nov. 2026. Europa Clipper is the largest spacecraft NASA has launched into deep space. It weighs about 12,800 pounds (6,000 kilograms) and is on a 1.8 billion-mile (2.9 billion-kilometer) trip to Jupiter. The Earth flyby is on Thursday, December 3, 2026, about 1,950 to 2,133 miles (3,140 to 3,450 kilometers) from Earth, with closest approach west of Africa at 3:14 p.m. EST. A gravity assist bends the path, adds speed, and saves propellant. The spacecraft passed 550 miles (884 kilometers) above Mars in March 2025. All nine science instruments will be on and collecting data, to compare with Earth data the team already has. A magnetometer measures magnetic fields and aims to help confirm an ocean under Europa’s ice. E-THEMIS sees heat in infrared light and will scan Earth every eight hours as the spacecraft gets closer. The spacecraft is scheduled to begin orbiting Jupiter in April 2030, then make many flybys of Europa. People near the path, mainly in southern Europe and Africa, may spot it with fairly large hobby telescopes. Whether that ocean has the ingredients for life is still unknown.

title: Europa Clipper
supports: Mission page, accessed 27 Nov. 2026. The trip is 1.8 billion miles (2.9 billion kilometers). Europa Clipper is scheduled to orbit Jupiter in April 2030 and then fly by Europa many times. The page describes an ocean that scientists think lies under Europa’s ice, and it points to the December 3, 2026 Earth flyby.

author: Trilaksono, W., Racho, A., Engilis, A., Hitch, A. T., & Herlambang, A. E. N.
title: Montane endemism and cryptic diversity in Sulawesi: A new species of flying frog with derived breeding traits
supports: Peer-reviewed description of Rhacophorus kurniatiae, published 11 Nov. 2026. Jelly egg masses on plants that hang above or near water; the paper says this way of laying eggs had not been recorded before among Sulawesi’s flying frogs. Rhacophorus boeadii is the close relative, and the DNA difference is small. The suggestion that jelly may help with ponds that come and go with the seasons still needs testing. The frog is described from this one high lake.

author: Dobbyn, Tiffany
title: New Asian Flying Frog Species Identified in Indonesia
supports: News report published 17 Nov. 2026. A small bright green frog, thousands of them around Danau Coca-Cola in the Mekongga Mountains, more than 6,100 feet above sea level, and Alan Hitch’s words about that pond. Flying frogs glide on large webbed feet and do not flap. Expeditions from 2009 to 2013 measured 28 body features, DNA, calls, and pointed snouts. Jelly eggs compared with foam nests, a cryptic species, and the name for Hellen Kurniati. The area is being considered as a national park, which has not happened yet. More species from these expeditions are still being described.
